slots.headline: No function in this contract lets an administrator move donor funds
slots.body: Three files on screen. ICampaign.sol defines the public API. Campaign.sol holds the escrow and the state machine. CampaignFactory.sol deploys 45-byte EIP-1167 clones. I will read the code line by line, then run make demo.
slots.citation-1: ICampaign.sol:7: Deliberately contains no function that lets an administrator move donor funds.
slots.citation-2: Campaign.sol:87-95: contribute() caps funding at the goal and records each donor's weight.
slots.citation-3: CampaignFactory.sol:36-67: createCampaign() validates inputs, deploys a clone, and initializes it in one transaction.

slots.headline: contribute() caps funding at the goal
slots.step-1: _sync() moves Funding to Active or Failed at the deadline, so no keeper or admin call is needed.
slots.step-2: WrongStatus reverts after the deadline or after activation.
slots.step-3: totalRaised + msg.value > goal reverts with GoalAlreadyReached, so no excess enters escrow.
slots.step-5: The contract adds to totalRaised and contributionOf, then emits Contributed. Only creator can call deliver(), which stores deliveredAt and opens the challenge window.
slots.diagram-caption: Campaign.sol:87-95 and 102-113. The onlyCreator modifier gates deliver() and withdraw(), and nothing else.

slots.headline: object() compares objection weight with half of totalRaised
slots.finding: The quorum line compares objectionWeight with half of totalRaised. release() has no access modifier because the caller has no choice of amount or destination.
slots.table-rows:
object()   uint256 weight = contributionOf[msg.sender];                        weight is fixed at funding time
object()   if (m.objectionWeight > totalRaised / 2)                             milestone Vetoed, campaign Canceled
release()  if (block.timestamp < deliveredAt + challengeWindow) revert           window must be closed
release()  m.mStatus = Released; creatorCredit += m.amount; ++releasedCount;     anyone may call; no privileged role
slots.source: Campaign.sol:121-140 and 145-165 · quorum is by money, not by donor count

slots.headline: Both payout functions update state before sending ETH
slots.step-1: claimRefund() rejects Funding, Active, and Completed, then reads the donor's exact contribution.
slots.step-2: The claim is zeroed and refundsWithdrawn increases before the transfer.
slots.step-3: msg.sender.call{value: amount} sends the ETH. A re-entry sees a settled claim and gets nothing.
slots.step-4: withdraw() is onlyCreator. It reads creatorCredit minus creatorWithdrawn, updates the ledger, then calls the creator.
slots.step-5: No function loops over donors, so one hostile recipient cannot block another recipient.
slots.diagram-caption: Campaign.sol:171-184 and 189-196. Checks, Effects, Interactions in that order.

slots.headline: The factory deploys clones and forwards the deposit
slots.implication-1: createCampaign() validates the deadline, goal, window, milestone count, sum, and exact deposit before it deploys a 45-byte EIP-1167 clone.
slots.implication-2: initialize() runs in the same transaction as clone creation, so no attacker can initialize a clone first. The factory forwards the deposit and never holds campaign ETH.
slots.limitation-1: A veto after a released milestone leaves refunds unfunded. The planned fix refunds only the unreleased remainder, pro rata.
slots.limitation-2: The deadline closes funding only. A creator who never delivers leaves funds in escrow. A delivery deadline is Week 4 work.
slots.future-work: Add the post-release veto regression, malicious reentrancy contracts, milestone fuzz handlers, and Sepolia deployment.
